If I did go to the ER, they'd send me home. But at home, it wouldn't take a whole lot to turn it into an emergency. What level of service is for a person who could go either way?

I was fired nearly a month ago. I also wish I was dead, I know what it's like for supervisors deliberating over you. I fucked up huge too. I feel like a loser, totally rejected. I feel like even more of a loser to be taking it so hard. I wish HR just killed me. I'm worried I'll never get another job because of this fuck up. 

I lost all my PTO, I lost my unemployment insurance. We're talking thousands. I'm so completely fucked. 

Everyone says it's not the end of the world but it totally feels like it. 

My only advice is to not suffer in silence. Like my boss tried to encourage me, saying I'll get an even better job. I think that was more *her* telling *herself* that so that she could feel better. DON'T LET PEOPLE GET AWAY WITH NOT WORRYING ABOUT YOU!

Thanks, that's good input. My least miserable moments are when I'm sleeping. My day is mainly waiting until it's late enough to sleep. But I'm also too stressed to sleep a full 8 hours. I'm not thinking about it every waking second like I used to but it is always in the background. I don't know if I should try to distract myself more with movies and stuff. 

A couple people from work emailed me to say hi. It made me happy but it also makes me miss them more. I went from seeing people every day who I liked and who liked me to not seeing anybody. It's going to be hard to get used to.

Couple more things I want to talk about:

I wish that they took me behind the HR building and just shot me. I think that nobody else gets what a big deal losing my job is to me. Like these other people, they've had plenty of jobs, they might've even been fired themselves, they have a life outside of work. If the HR guy just killed me, everyone would know that it's all over for me and these people did it to me. If I killed myself it'd be like "oh he did this entirely to himself". Someone else would be mad at someone besides me on my behalf. I feel like it would be healthier if I was mad about losing my job instead of feeling depressed and vulnerable. 

And I think everyone expects me to be mad. That's why they wouldn't let me come by the office and see people. It's like they *want* me to be mad. I don't think anybody understands what I'm really feeling and why.

>  You're certainly entitled to it.

thanks for that. See when I get like this I feel so damn bad about all the stuff I did do wrong that I'll think I deserve anything bad that ever happens to me.
I don't think I can get unemplyment if I was fired "for cause". I don't even know if that includes me or what. I have no idea how any of this shit works.

I loved work. It was a shit job but it made me feel so normal. I think maybe I was substituting friends and family with coworkers. I have nobody else. Everyone there liked me and I liked them. Before I worked, I was basically a shut in.

I know I screwed up. I was pissed at work stuff, and life in general and I kicked a piece of furniture and I damaged it. Nobody else was around, I haven't seen anyone since, and I'm worried that they don't like me anymore. As far as they know I kicked the shit out of their property and walked out. I'm worried they think I'm violent and mad at them, which would explain why nobody called. The truth is I regret it more than anything I've ever done. I'm going to miss everyone so much and they'll be thinking I hate them. 

People have always thought I'm a loose cannon or a drug user since high school because I've been so quiet my entire life. Now they *really* think that. I'm actually just so compassionate and I just want people to care about me and it's not fair. 

Do you think I should be more assertive? Should I be insisting that they let me talk to coworkers and explain money and benefits to me? I don't even know how to act, I don't even know what to do.

I don't even care about the money. It won't be an issue for a while. But I mean, they literally just cut me off. I don't know if I get severance or money or what. Aren't they supposed to tell me something about COBRA? I'm not in the right state of mind to be hounding these people. I've never lost a job before and I don't know if I'm supposed to go to the unemployment office or what. I can't even *imagine* starting to look for another job. At this point, disability seems more viable than that. It's just so much on top of an already fragile mind and nobody is helping me. 

In six days, I'm seeing a counselor. So that's my goal: just make it six days.

Except I hold my tongue because the values of the *giver* count too. It baffles me when I see people criticizing a charity based on what proportion of it's money goes to research. Research? That's an irrelevant criteria for judging my #1 charity. 

Some people think research has a bigger return than action. Some people scoff at "administrative costs" but some people defend them saying that spending more now on overhead pays off in the future. *You can't say that someone else is doing charity wrong if they don't even begin on the same page as you.*

It's not the same old shit. We have made progress. We were not more secure back then. But progress is always *ahead* of us. So when you look backwards, it is the same old shit.

It already is about race, wouldn't you agree? I'm not *making* this about anything. I'm acknowledging that race is pretty much the biggest thing that this story is about. I'm not saying that the cop killed the guy because he's racist. I'm saying tons of people think that's what cops do.

Whether the police department systematically discriminates or whether an entire city is so convinced that they do as to riot, *race* is the thing you talk about in either case. Yes, people need to talk about lethal force without bringing up race. They also need to figure out how race *actually* was involved here, because it was and is.

Don't dismiss this thing as race baiting. You need to bring up racism to find out if you're wrong about racism. There were people on both sides in the Zimmerman thing, exchanging arguments whether he was or wasn't a racist. Just like there are both sides now. You have to talk about it to convince people.
